articles.title: Cornell rape accuser can remain 'Jane Doe' as judge warns threats could lead to federal charges
articles.summary: A New York judge ruled the Cornell Jane Doe accuser can keep her pseudonym in the civil case against Chi Phi fraternity members she accused of rape.
articles.body: A judge has allowed the former Cornell student who sued the Chi Phi fraternity members over rape allegations to continue using the pseudonym "Jane Doe." New York Supreme Court Justice Phaedra Perry-Bond, who is presiding over the civil case, said in a Friday order that Jane Doe had argued that publicly identifying her could expose her to "retribution and retaliation," hinder her social life and career, and cause shame to her family. Doe also told the court that she fears being identified would lead to her family being placed in danger, adding that she has "experienced extreme anxiety, depression, and insomnia." None of the defendants opposed Doe's request to continue using a pseudonym, according to the order. CORNELL UNIVERSITY BANS FRATERNITY PARTIES FOR THE REST OF THE YEAR AFTER SEX ABUSE LAWSUIT Ultimately, the judge ruled that Doe's privacy interests outweighed the normal presumption that court proceedings should be fully public, especially given "the notoriety of the allegations" and "the widespread reports of certain malicious actors' behavior in attempting to threaten and retaliate against anyone tangentially involved in this case." In an unusual move, the judge included a sort of public service announcement in her order, warning that attempts to harass or threaten Doe, the defendants or attorneys involved in the case could constitute a federal crime and lead to prosecution. Perry-Bond also noted that allowing Doe to use a pseudonym would preserve public access to the case without resorting to more restrictive measures, such as sealing the court docket or closing the courtroom. While Doe will remain anonymous publicly, the individually named defendants will continue to be identified in court filings. CORNELL SEXUAL ASSAULT CASE REVIVES SCRUTINY OF A LITTLE-KNOWN NEW YORK LAW ON INTOXICATED VICTIMS However, Perry-Bond said protections for sensitive personal information, such as home addresses, phone numbers and email addresses, should also be extended to the individually named defendants. She invited the parties to propose an agreement providing similar protections to defendants and potentially other people involved in the case. Doe filed her lawsuit in September, accusing seven former Chi Phi fraternity members of drugging and raping her on the night of Oct. 19, 2024, and into the next morning. The complaint also names the fraternity itself, the university, and the bar Doe went to the night of the alleged gang rape. In the lawsuit, she alleges she was already intoxicated when she arrived at the fraternity house, where the men then pressured her to take ketamine and other substances. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some saying any sexual activity was consensual and others denying they were involved. BAR NAMED IN CORNELL RAPE LAWSUIT DISPUTES ACCUSER'S ACCOUNT, SAYS SHE WAS NEVER SERVED ALCOHOL WHILE UNDERAGE The fraternity was suspended on Nov. 8, 2024, the same day Doe reported sexual assault allegations to campus police, according to Doe's civil complaint. Local prosecutor Matthew Van Houten, who intially declined to pursue criminal charges, has said Doe's sworn statement from November 2024 did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped. That statement, Van Houten said, described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual." However, CBS New York later obtained the transcript of the Cornell police interviews with Doe on Nov. 14 and 15, 2024, during which she told investigators: "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped." SALLY YATES' CORNELL REVIEW OF ALLEGED GANG RAPE COULD SCRUTINIZE CRUCIAL POLICE INTERVIEW, ATTORNEY SAYS Van Houten said he was never given this full transcript. He announced late last month that his office was reopening the investigation after allegations made in Doe's lawsuit differed from those in her sworn statement nearly two years earlier. Days after Van Houten reversed course, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul removed him from the case, citing her lack of confidence in his judgment, and appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor. James' appointment has also drawn controversy, with multiple defendants seeking her removal over alleged bias stemming largely from a social media post she made days before her appointment that they argue showed sympathy for Jane Doe. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP On Thursday, James filed a response in court, arguing that the defendants have no standing and that even if they did, the governor has the power to appoint a special prosecutor. A separate motion from another defendant, a former fraternity member, asked the state Supreme Court to disqualify James from any future grand jury proceedings, arguing that her public comments had prejudiced potential grand jurors and undermined the fairness of the process. That matter remains pending.

articles.title: John Wick at 12: The action franchise that forced us to look at grief better than most dramas
articles.summary: When John Wick hit theaters on October 24, 2014, most of us expected the film to be another slick, gun-heavy action movie, albeit with the star power of
articles.body: When John Wick hit theaters on October 24, 2014, most of us expected the film to be another slick, gun-heavy action movie, albeit with the star power of Keanu Reeves – an actor whose credentials as an action star was already established. Twelve years later, it’s a global blockbuster phenomenon. We still can’t get enough of John Wick.But is it the action sequences that draw us into theatre halls? Or, is it that the movie stirred something so deep and visceral in us that we didn’t see coming. Released as an action film with “gun-fu” stunts ( hybrid action style that blends close-quarters firearm use with traditional martial arts, acrobatics, and choreographed melee combat), John Wick tapped something far deeper – the unbearable pain of loss, death.And the void we find ourselves in even as we try to get by because the world has gotten too comfortable with the adage: Move on. John Wick did something no one was expecting. It got grief better than most Hollywood tearjerkers.While traditional action movies use a personal tragedy as a quick excuse for revenge, this film turns loss into the whole emotional engine of the story. It hits home with audiences far beyond hardcore action fans because it captures a raw truth: grief isn’t a neat, step-by-step process toward closure. It’s a relentless, crushing force that changes your life forever.A cold world and relentless sorrowIt is a particularly important lesson in our times as our preparedness or ability to grapple with difficult emotions have diminished over the past decade and a half or so. To that extent this Keanu-Reeves starrer was well ahead of its time. As most art is. It came at a time when technology was developing so rapidly that in a few years it would completely take hold over our minds and even control our emotions (read rage-bait).Neurologists and psychologists, backed by research, have been telling us for the past few years that social media and addiction to smartphones and gadgets have made us more vulnerable than we ever knew. Each and everyone of us is struggling to deal with the smallest of infractions to the biggest mistakes – because our reaction to everything is too loud, too angry and too out of our control.Hence John Wick—whicever chapter—we are watching is a special kind of catharsis we are looking for. Wick’s action and the attacks on him all seem a bit too much. Why is everyone against a grieving man, who just wanted to be left alone? Does that seem familiar?It’s because for a second it felt it was you. It could be me. It is, actually, everyone.Then there is the matter of a lovely little puppy.“It wasn’t just a dog”The setup for the first film—a bad guy killing an adorable Beagle puppy, Daisy, almost didn’t happen. Studio executives panicked, warning directors Chad Stahelski and David Leitch that killing a puppy would alienate the audience. But lead actor Keanu Reeves fought hard to keep the scene, knowing the entire heart of the movie rested on it. Maybe Reeves is a canny businessman. A good storyteller. A great actor whose face can portray rage and grief in the same frame like very few others. Or, maybe he knew something about the coming decade. Or, is just just understanding human fallibility?In the first film, released today 12 years ago, when John later tells a criminal boss, “it wasn't just a dog,” he sums up the whole franchise.Before she died of a terminal illness, John’s wife Helen knew her husband—a former hitman used to total control—would lock himself away in silent despair. So, she arranged for Daisy to be delivered to him after her death as a final gift. The puppy was a lifeline, a gentle way for John to heal without destroying himself.So when a degenerate mobster breaks into John’s house and slaughters Daisy, he isn’t just stealing a car or hurting a pet; he’s ripping away John’s only safe outlet for mourning. With his quiet healing stolen, John’s buried pain erupts. The return of his deadly assassin persona, ‘Baba Yaga,’ isn’t a cool victory — it’s a painful relapse. The explosion of violence is his way of screaming against an unbearable void.Throughout the series, John’s grief reshapes how he fits into his world. The secret assassin underworld—with its High Table rules, gold coins, and neutral Continental hotels—acts like a mirror for a cold society that only cares about deals and rules.The High Table demands order. But grief is unpredictable and absolute. When a mob boss tries to bribe and/or reason with John, he fails to realize that money and power mean nothing to a man who has lost his reason to live.John sledgehammers everything — from his basement to his enemies because emotional pain cannot be bought off or negotiated.Revenge gives grief a direction for John. It turns helplessness into action. Sorrow into purpose. John knows how to kill; he does not know how to live with the absence of the person who made his life worth living. The first film's tragedy is that the world he escaped offers him a familiar language for his pain, and it is the only language he knows how to speak.When grief becomes a way of lifeWhat makes the subsequent films so compelling is that they refuse to treat revenge as a clean emotional transaction. Killing the people responsible does not restore Helen, nor does it return John to the life he had before her death. Instead, every act of violence draws him deeper into the world he had abandoned. In John Wick: Chapter 2, the consequences of his return become impossible to contain; in John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum, survival itself becomes an exhausting, almost mechanical exercise. The action expands, but the emotional possibilities contract.This is where the franchise's relentlessness becomes more than a stylistic signature. John rarely has the luxury of stopping long enough to consider what his actions mean. Enemies arrive before he can recover from the last fight, obligations accumulate, and the machinery of violence keeps moving.It resembles the way grief can overwhelm a person's inner life, occupying so much mental and emotional space that ordinary existence begins to feel remote. Kind of what our lives look like since 2020. Post Covid. We are talking of mass PTSD – undeclared medically but feels real enough.The comparison is not literal, of course, but the films capture something recognisable about the experience of being unable to put down an emotion that has become the organising principle of one's life.There is also a darker suggestion here: that grief and anger contain an enormous, often destructive potential when they are given no other outlet. John's extraordinary abilities make him almost superhuman, but they do not make him emotionally invulnerable. If anything, his competence is part of the problem. He can turn pain into action with terrifying efficiency, yet he cannot make the pain disappear. The world sees a legendary assassin; we see a man who has never quite found a way back from loss.The fourth film brings this preoccupation with mortality to the foreground. Reeves has explained that death and the possibility of peace became central to the story they wanted to tell, giving John's journey a destination beyond another cycle of revenge.The question is no longer simply whether John can defeat his enemies, but whether there is any way for him to escape the life that grief has helped set in motion.In the end that is the paradox at the heart of the film. John Wick keeps going because stopping would mean facing the silence left behind by Helen. And that silence, more than any army of assassins, is the one adversary he has never quite learned to defeat.That is too familiar an emotion for all of us, especially, in the times we live in.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jordan’s King Abdullah orders firm response after deadly church attack
articles.summary: Authorities searching for attackers say too early to determine if they had ties to known groups, as death toll now nine.
articles.body:
Jordan’s King Abdullah has ordered security forces to respond firmly and pursue those behind a church attack in the Karak governorate that killed nine people and wounded 40, the royal court has said.

The country has already increased security across malls, foreign embassies and other locations across the country in response to the attack, according to the US embassy in Amman, as authorities continue to search for the perpetrators.

On Friday, assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, about 120km (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman, in what Jordanian authorities described as an “act of extremist terrorism”.

Eight people were confirmed dead on Friday, with authorities saying one more succumbed to their injuries on Saturday. “The death toll from the terrorist act in Karak has risen to nine after one of the wounded died,” state news agency Petra reported, citing Jordan Public Security.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, as Jordan declared three days of national mourning, according to Petra.

King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against violent armed groups in the region, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished “with an iron fist”.

Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said on X that the attack was “a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism”.

“We will not allow society to go down this path,” he added.

Authorities said they were still searching for the attackers, adding that it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.

Video footage showed police patrolling outside the church on Saturday.

Nasser al-Burqan, a survivor of the attack, told the Reuters news agency that one of the attackers, standing about two metres (6.5 feet) away, pointed a handgun at him and opened fire on Friday.

A short while later, his son, who also attended the mass, called him to say he had been shot in the leg and was being treated in hospital.

“When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me, and I saw two [assailants] — one was masked, the other was not; he was carrying a handgun,” said al-Burqan, a lawyer.

“A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word,” said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin’s was injured in the attack.

Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor of Shihan village in Karak, joined a list of officials condemning what he called a “wicked” attack.

“God willing, this country will remain safe,” he said.

Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by violent groups motivated by a strict interpretation of Islam in recent years.

Karak is home to a minority Christian population in Jordan, and the country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.

articles.title: Louvre turns away tourists as Paris braces for renewed violence following destructive riots
articles.summary: Tourists were turned away from the Louvre as heightened security measures, nationwide demonstrations and fears of further unrest disrupted travel and major cultural attractions across Paris.
articles.body: Tourists were turned away from the Louvre on Saturday as some of Paris' most iconic museums remained shuttered amid fears of renewed violence, a week after destructive riots erupted across France. The Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais were all shuttered Saturday as French officials prepared for another weekend of potentially violent demonstrations, according to The Associated Press (AP). Visitors were seen peering through the Louvre's locked gates Saturday, where a posted notice announced its temporary closure. TOP TOURIST DESTINATION IN THE WORLD SHUTS DOWN AMID VIOLENT PROTESTS The museum, home to Leonardo da Vinci's famed "Mona Lisa," was among several major attractions closed amid fears of violent protests. French officials planned to deploy up to 70,000 law enforcement officers nationwide on Saturday, supported by helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons, according to the AP. The closures came as protesters gathered across France on Saturday, with police rerouting Paris' main demonstration away from the city center to prevent another outbreak of violence. FURIOUS CROWDS PROTEST SKY-HIGH HOUSING COSTS AND MASS TOURISM IN MAJOR CITY Shopkeepers were seen boarding up storefronts across Paris, while police stood guard beneath the Arc de Triomphe as authorities braced for another round of unrest. The closures also disrupted Art Basel Paris, a major international art fair held at the Grand Palais. It had opened to the public Friday before organizers canceled the weekend program over security concerns. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The precautions followed a weekend of violent demonstrations that left approximately 3,000 businesses across France damaged or looted, according to the AP. The Louvre had already been forced to close earlier in the week after student protesters blocked access to the museum, Fox News Digital previously reported. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Visitors arriving at the Louvre on Monday morning were met with barricades at the museum's iconic glass pyramid, Carrousel du Louvre and Passage Richelieu entrances, as protesters from the École du Louvre blocked access, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP). The blockade forced museum officials to turn away visitors from the popular attraction, which draws as many as 20,000 people on its busiest days, according to French media reports. "You are giving Paris a terrible image." Earlier this week, tourists were left frustrated after being turned away from the Louvre, with one Dutch couple calling the closure "shameful," according to French newspaper Le Monde. "You are giving Paris a terrible image," the couple said as they held up their tickets. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The U.S. Embassy in France has warned Americans to steer clear of violent protests as widespread unrest prompted curfews and raised concerns about travel disruptions across the country. The embassy said in a Monday statement that partial curfews had been introduced in several French cities, with additional restrictions possible. Travelers visiting Paris this week were advised to avoid popular protest gathering spots, including Place de la République, Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation, along with major thoroughfares such as Boulevard Voltaire, which are frequently used for demonstrations, per The Times of London. articles.title: College football's NIL and transfer portal chaos on display as nation's top receiver holds absurd ceremony
articles.summary: On the fourth Saturday of October, Oregon State's Jesse Legree held a signing ceremony to announce he's staying with the Beavers next season.
articles.body: It's the fourth Saturday of October, folks. Wake up! It's another college football gameday! The season is just over the halfway point, and the temperature has been cranked way up. We've got conference races coming down to the wire. Playoff hopefuls in must-win situations. Arch Manning might get benched? Half the top 10 teams in the country lost last weekend. It's just chaos everywhere you look right now, which is why college football is, by far, the best sport in America. SEC'S CRAZY, HISTORY-MAKING WEEK 7 WEEKEND IS THE LATEST EXAMPLE OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S NEW ERA Now, with all that being said, it's also the dumbest sport in America — mainly due to the horrible NIL and transfer portal landscape that we've all created. And for those who don't believe me, here's Oregon State freshman star Jesse Legree — who is also one of the top receivers in the country — taking time out of his busy week of practice to hold a signing ceremony at his high school to announce ... ... that he's signing BACK with the Beavers for next season. Take a look: At least Jesse Legree is going back to school! "What is the major announcement you want to make to the country?" the CBS fellas ask Legree, who is stationed at St. Francis Academy with what sounds like a big crowd on hand. COUNTRY STAR, FORMER COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYER LEE BRICE RIPS NIL, PRO PLAYERS GOING BACK TO COLLEGE "I will be signing with the Oregon State Beavers for the 2027-2028 season," Legree, who currently plays for the OREGON STATE BEAVERS, said. Look, college football is so broken off the field at this point, I'm not even sure where we go from here. The product on the field is excellent. It's the best show on turf right now, and that includes the NFL. HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL But off the field? It's such a joke. This is so absurd, I don't even know where to begin. To channel my inner Mike Gundy: CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Where are we at in society today?!" Holding a news conference, calling the local TV stations, and announcing to "the country" that you're ... returning to your school next season ... is everything wrong with the current college football landscape. It feels like an SNL parody. Sadly, it's not. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And by the way, this has nothing to do with Jesse Legree, the player. He's arguably the best wide receiver in the country not named Jeremiah Smith. The freshman currently leads the nation in receiving yards (1,040), touchdown catches (14) and yards per game (148.6). Not bad! It's only natural that folks would speculate that he's probably hitting the portal next season and going to an LSU, or Notre Dame, or Miami, or Ohio State. I get it. And honestly, good on Legree for actually returning to Oregon State. You NEVER see kids dance with the partners they came with anymore. They're all one-and-done. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Not Legree. Good for him. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP I just don't know that we needed all the theatrics that came with it.

articles.title: Bhutanese man shot and killed during robbery attempt at his jewelry store in Ohio, immigrant business owners say they are scared
articles.summary: Tara Sinchuri, a Bhutanese man, was found dead inside his jewelry store along Dixie Highway in Fairfield, Ohio, in what cops believe was a robbery attempt.
articles.body: Tara Sinchuri, a Bhutanese man, was found dead inside his jewelry store along Dixie Highway in Fairfield, Ohio, in what cops believe was a robbery attempt. The incident took place on Tuesday as the Hindu Bhutanese-Nepalese community was preparing for Vijayadashami. No suspect has been arrested even four days after the broad daylight shooting.Sinchuri was widely known in his community. Tara Dahal, a friend, said he had a great contribution towards the Bhutanese community in Cincinnati. "He is very social, very helpful, and I have known him for several years back from Nepal. We were neighbors in Nepal also, so he is a very kind-hearted man. He used to help us in the community in various community events. He had donated. So he has a great contribution to the Bhutanese community here in Cincinnati," Dahal said, adding that this was probably the first time some one from their community had been shot and killed in an incident like this.Dahal said to local television channel WCPO 9 News that the incident scared other immigrant business owners in the area. "People come to the U.S. to make their life, make their dream true… I was talking with some of the owners here, business owners nearby… They were very scared. They are very afraid," Dahal said.On Friday, friends and family members gathered outside the jewelry store for a vigil where the community leader was fondly remembered."Not only just in Ohio but in the entire United States, he has been an influence on our community. He has provided for those in need," Tara Sinchuri's nephew Anish Sinchuri said. "What has happened to him is gruesome. It is crazy. It's absolutely shocking for our family, our entire family," he said.The family has set up a fundraiser on GoFundMe to pay for his funeral and other related expenses."He born in Bhutan in 1974. Immigrated to the United States in 2009. He was raising a beautiful family in Fairfield Township: one son, two daughters, and his caring wife. He was an active community member, philanthropist, and public speaker. He also holds board membership on several community- and religious-based nonprofit organizations. He was truly a role model to Bhutanese Nepali immigrant communities in the United States," the fundraiser said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: British police received allegations about Meghan’s father in 2019 but didn’t tell other forces
articles.summary: LONDON — Police in the British capital said Saturday that they received a letter containing allegations about the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019, but did not tell other law enforcement agencies.
articles.body: LONDON — Police in the British capital said Saturday that they received a letter containing allegations about the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019, but did not tell other law enforcement agencies. Authorities in the Philippines confirmed this week that they are investigating Thomas Markle over claims that he kept child sexual abuse images at his home. He has denied the allegations. Meghan said in a statement Friday that she was “deeply distressed” by the allegations and that she was previously informed by police of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018. A spokesperson for London’s Metropolitan Police said a review of records confirmed that the force received a letter in January 2019 “containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.” “It was sent to the MPS Protection Command to raise concerns in relation to the security of the Duchess of Sussex,” the statement added. “The letter was reviewed and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness. The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.” The statement did not say whether any investigation took place or if any further action was taken. The force said it was reviewing the incident and considering whether to refer itself to the United Kingdom’s Independent Office for Police Conduct. Asked about the discrepancy between the two statements on the date of the letter, a spokesperson for Meghan told NBC News she “may have been mistaken by a few months.” The allegations against Thomas Markle were first reported Thursday by The Sun, a British tabloid, which reported that his son had informed police after he said he found “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images in boxes at his father’s home. The Sun published a photo it said showed the son, Thomas Markle Jr., signing a sworn statement it said he had submitted to police and quoted him as saying: “I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him.” In a statement Friday, Meghan addressed the report that her father was being investigated. “The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” said Meghan, whose relationship with her father has been limited and fraught in recent years. He did not attend her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, drawing widespread media scrutiny. She said the letter sent to the British police and other authorities in 2018 “made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.” Meghan added that she had chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father “for one reason: to protect them.” The elder Markle, 82, denied the reported allegations, calling them “sick lies” in a statement to Britain’s Daily Mail newspaper. He added they were “the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.” His daughter Samantha Markle also dismissed her brother’s allegations, telling the Daily Mail that “there is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever. ... He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.” NBC News did not immediately receive responses to requests for comment from Markle Jr. or Samantha Markle — Meghan’s half-siblings. NBC News was not immediately able to identify a contact for Markle Sr., who the Daily Mail reported was now in a Florida rehab center recovering from surgery. In a statement, the FBI said it was “aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of U.S. law.” The Philippines’ justice department confirmed Friday that “the matter is under investigation” but otherwise declined to “provide further details at this time.” Meghan, 45, and Harry, 42, moved back to the United Kingdom earlier this summer after several years in the United States. The couple last week made their first joint public appearance since returning to the U.K., visiting charities in central England. King Charles III has made clear that their return does not signal a return to active royal life. Harry, however, has said recently that he wants his disagreements with his family to “work out.”

articles.title: 45 paise for Rs 10 lakh cover: Railways extends insurance to counter tickets from October 27
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Indian Railways has decided to extend its Optional Travel Insurance Scheme (OTIS) to passengers booking reserved tickets through Passenger
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Indian Railways has decided to extend its Optional Travel Insurance Scheme (OTIS) to passengers booking reserved tickets through Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counters from October 27, in compliance with Supreme Court directions.In an order issued on Saturday, the Railway Board directed all zonal railways to make necessary arrangements for implementing the scheme at reservation counters.The decision follows the Supreme Court's October 6 order in the Union of India versus Radha Yadav case.Under the scheme, passengers can opt for insurance by paying a premium of 45 paise per passenger, offering coverage of up to Rs 10 lakh in case of death or permanent total disability arising from a railway accident or untoward incident.The policy also provides Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability, up to Rs 2 lakh towards hospitalisation expenses and Rs 10,000 for transportation of mortal remains.According to the Railway Board, insurance will remain optional, and reservation staff must inform passengers about its availability before booking.Passengers opting for insurance must provide a mobile number and pay the premium through digital payment modes only. The premium will be collected along with the ticket fare.Insurance policy details will be communicated to passengers through their registered mobile numbers.The Board clarified that the existing terms and conditions applicable to IRCTC e-ticket insurance will also apply to tickets purchased at reservation counters.Divisional railway managers and commercial officers have been directed to monitor implementation, while zonal railways must submit compliance reports confirming operational readiness.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Who was behind the deadly church shooting in Jordan?
articles.summary: Authorities are investigating the rare attack on a Christian church; the assailants remain unidentified and at large.
articles.body:
Security forces in Jordan are searching for three gunmen who opened fire at a church in Karak governorate on Friday, killing eight people and injuring dozens more, according to Jordan’s Ministry of Health.

King Abdullah II said those behind the attack would face the “harshest penalties”, as he offered his condolences to the victims’ families. He has ordered a review of the country’s security procedures for responding to terrorist attacks.

Authorities are calling this rare attack on a Christian place of worship an act of terror, with the perpetrators yet to be identified.

Here’s what we know about how the attack unfolded, and what was behind it.

What happened during the church shooting in Karak?

On Friday afternoon, three masked gunmen opened fire during a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud.

Survivors said they heard an explosion just after the start of the service. Two attackers who arrived in a vehicle were joined by a third carrying a semi-automatic rifle. They entered the church and opened fire for several minutes.

One survivor, Nasser al-Burqan, a lawyer, told the Reuters news agency that one of the attackers, standing about two metres (6.5 feet) away, pointed a handgun at him and opened fire.

“When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me, and I saw two [assailants] – one was masked, the other was not; he was carrying a handgun,” said al-Burqan, a lawyer.

Later, his son, who had also been present, called him to say he had been shot in the leg and was being treated in hospital.

Tarek Ammarin, who was visiting a relative injured in the attack, now in hospital, said: “A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word.”

Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor of Shihan village in Karak, joined a list of officials condemning what he called a “wicked” attack.

“God willing, this country will remain safe,” he said.

State news channel Al-Mamlaka reported that security forces were deployed to the church and were in pursuit of the two suspects who had arrived in a vehicle.

Eight people were killed in the shooting, including seven who died at the scene and one who succumbed to her injuries hours after the attack, Jordan’s Petra news agency reported on Saturday.

Of the 40 people injured, 27 are still in hospital. The Director of Prince Ali Military Hospital in Karak said one person is in critical condition, after undergoing surgery.

The identity of the three attackers has not been confirmed, with government statements referring to them as “unknown assailants”.

Security camera footage of the attack has been circulating online, however. Video broadcast by Al-Mamlaka shows three people shooting outside the church and running towards its entrance.

Other footage also shows the attackers opening fire on a group of men outside the building trying to flee.

Jordan’s Interior Minister Mazin Al-Farrayeh said a group of “extremists” that have “no relationship to humanity” were responsible for the attack, though no specific groups were mentioned.

Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said on Friday that the attack was a by-product of terrorist ideology and “blind extremism”, but did not give specifics about the attackers.

The motive remains unclear since the attackers’ identities have yet to be revealed.

Where is Karak, and what do we know about its Christian community?

Karak governorate is about 120km (75 miles) south of Amman and is home to many from Jordan’s Christian minority, which makes up about 300,000 of the country’s population of 11.5 million people.

Taylor Luck, senior Middle East correspondent at the Christian Science Monitor, told Al Jazeera that Jordan’s Christians “pride themselves on [their] interfaith solidarity and coexistence”.

He said that Christians and Muslims have lived side-by-side in Karak for generations and that if the attack had been carried out in an attempt to divide the community, it is more likely that the “community come[s] back even stronger”.

Jordan is also home to many biblical sites that draw visitors from around the world.

What has the response been to this shooting?

Several countries, including Azerbaijan, Iraq, Poland, Palestine and Qatar, have issued statements condemning the attack and expressing their solidarity with Jordan.

Ahmed al-Tayeb, the grand imam of Al-Azhar in Cairo, a leading Sunni religious institution, offered his condolences to the families of the victims, calling the shooting a “heinous terrorist attack”.

“This crime contradicts the teachings of the Abrahamic religions and reveals that its perpetrators are devoid of all compassion, humanity and morality,” he wrote in a social media post.

The United States embassy in Jordan also released a statement on X offering condolences to victims and survivors of the attack.

“On behalf of the American people, we offer our most heartfelt condolences to the victims and survivors of the terror attack today at a church in Karak, Jordan,” it said.

The Jordanian Prime Minister declared three days of mourning following the attack, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public buildings.

Has Jordan experienced similar attacks before?

In 2016, the ISIL (ISIS) group carried out a series of attacks across Karak, including a deadly siege on a Crusader-era castle in which 10 people were killed, including a Canadian tourist and seven police officers. Dozens of others were injured.

Four attackers were later killed by Jordanian security forces following a long standoff.

articles.title: In 2020, Selena Gomez bought a California mansion once owned by music legend Tom Petty for $4.89 million; six years later, she sold the nearly 11,500-square-foot estate for $5.4 million after buying a $35 million marital home
articles.summary: Selena Gomez sold her Encino, California, mansion for $5.399 million, six years after purchasing the property for $4.895 million.
articles.body: Selena Gomez sold her Encino, California, mansion for $5.399 million, six years after purchasing the property for $4.895 million. The nearly 11,500-square-foot estate was once owned by rock musician Tom Petty and later became the filming location for the first three seasons of Gomez’s cooking series, ‘Selena + Chef.’As reported by Realtor, the singer sold the six-bedroom property on September 8, 2026, after listing it in May for nearly $6.5 million. The final sale price was about $1.1 million below the original asking price. The sale comes after Gomez and her husband, music producer Benny Blanco, purchased a $35 million estate in Beverly Hills in December 2024, shortly before announcing their engagement. The couple married in September 2025.Selena Gomez bought the mansion for $4.89 million in 2020Gomez purchased the Encino home in March 2020 for $4.895 million, according to the Los Angeles Times. The property sits on nearly an acre of land and was custom-built for Petty and his first wife, Jane Benyo, in 1989. The home had a turbulent history before Gomez acquired it. A fire in 1987 destroyed most of the original structure, leaving the basement recording studio largely intact. Petty rebuilt the three-storey house, which was completed two years later.Petty and Benyo later separated, and the property passed through several owners. It was sold again in 2017 and underwent extensive renovation before Gomez bought it in 2020. The house’s original music connection remained one of its distinctive features. The lower level included a recording studio and vocal booth, along with a wine cellar, gym, massage room and other entertainment spaces.A mansion with six bedrooms, a pool and a recording studioThe estate measures approximately 11,500 square feet and has six bedrooms. As reported by Realtor, it had multiple bedroom suites, a gourmet kitchen, a formal dining room, a family room and a spacious living area with high ceilings. The kitchen features marble countertops, an island and a brick stove. Other amenities include a media room, office, gym, wine cellar and massage room.Outside, the grounds include a swimming pool and spa, a cabana, a fire pit and areas for outdoor dining. A waterfall and stream also form part of the landscaped backyard. The house was more than a residence for Selena. According to Architectural Digest, the kitchen served as the filming location for the first three seasons of her HBO Max cooking series, ‘Selena + Chef,’ in which she prepared meals with guidance from professional chefs.Why she sold it below the original asking priceGomez listed the Encino property for approximately $6.495 million in May 2026. The home attracted a buyer after an earlier pending deal fell through in July, according to ELLE Decor. It ultimately sold on September 8 for $5.399 million. The sale price was around $504,000 more than the $4.895 million Gomez paid in 2020, before accounting for transaction costs, taxes, maintenance, renovation expenses or other ownership costs. The final price was also about $1.1 million below the original asking price, a reduction of roughly 17%.The $35 million Beverly Hills home she shares with Benny BlancoGomez and Blanco purchased their Beverly Hills residence in December 2024 for $35 million, according to Realtor. The property includes a main house and two guesthouses, one of which has a studio and another a home theatre. The estate also has a fitness centre, swimming pool, greenhouse and landscaped outdoor spaces. Its size and facilities make it substantially larger than the Encino property Gomez has now sold.The Beverly Hills purchase took place shortly before the couple announced their engagement in December 2024. They married in September 2025.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: In 2015, a Florida couple bought a 210-acre farm near Gainesville and rescued three cows; 10 years later, Critter Creek Farm Sanctuary spans 420 acres and is home to more than 180 cows, donkeys, pigs and other rescued animals
articles.summary: When Erin and Chris Amerman purchased a 210-acre farm near Gainesville, Florida, in 2015, they had no idea how much their rescue efforts would grow.
articles.body: When Erin and Chris Amerman purchased a 210-acre farm near Gainesville, Florida, in 2015, they had no idea how much their rescue efforts would grow. A year later, they turned it into Critter Creek Farm Sanctuary. They started with three rescued cows. By 2019, they had expanded their mission by acquiring Critter Hills, a 200-acre ranch and hay farm in nearby Alachua. Today, the sanctuary spans three properties totalling 420 acres and cares for more than 180 cows, alongside donkeys, pigs, horses, a bison, a turkey and a water buffalo. The sanctuary is more than a haven for rescued animals. Of the original property, 125 acres are dedicated to wildlife conservation, while monthly tours and public events help visitors connect with farmed animals!The rat who changed everythingErin Amerman’s road to rescue started with a rat. She was seven, and her mother had finally agreed to let her have her first pet. Erin wanted a hamster. During a visit to the pet shop, she realised that the hamster she picked up wanted to pee on her. Another wanted to bite her. A third only wanted to run away from her as fast as it could. That was when a young woman working at the shop asked if she had ever considered a rat. Erin and her mother were surprised. They wondered whether rats made good pets. The woman told them that rats were gentle, intelligent animals that rarely got a fair chance because people assumed they were dirty and dangerous. Erin held one, and he was sweet. But he did pee on her! Guess which animal came home? Not the hamster, but the sweet little rat she named Templeton! Besides peeing on her, Templeton also taught her something priceless: how society treats two species of animals differently. Hamsters are welcomed into homes, while rats are often feared or rejected. This very incident led her to co-found Critter Creek Farm Sanctuary with her husband, Chris Amerman, in 2016.They started with three cowsErin met Chris Amerman at the University of West Florida in 1995. Two years later, they exchanged their wedding vows. Chris, who has always been an animal lover, gave up animal products shortly afterwards. While they were in medical school, the couple started volunteering at a no-kill shelter. They began rescuing cats and dogs, and they never stopped.In 2015, they purchased the original 210-acre Critter Creek farm and wildlife preserve near Gainesville, Florida. A year later, they founded Critter Creek Farm Sanctuary, a non-profit organisation that began with three rescued cows. It is a farmed-animal sanctuary, wildlife refuge and community organisation. “Our mission is to foster compassion for all animals through science-based rescue, outreach and conservation,” they state on their website. Today, it has grown into the largest bovine sanctuary in the US, with three facilities totalling 420 acres. The land has become a home for animals that had nowhere else to go. Keeping a rescue running takes space, and space costs money. In 2019, the Amermans gave up the dream house they had been saving for. Instead, they put that money towards Critter Hills, a 200-acre ranch and hay farm in Alachua. “We realised that if we’re going to keep this rescue thing going, well, we’re gonna need a bigger ark.”The rescuesToday, Critter Creek Farm Sanctuary is home to more than 180 cows, making it the largest cow sanctuary in the country. People have asked them why they focus on cows, and they have a reason. Cows need a lot of room, live a long time with good care and require plenty of food. Many rescues simply can’t take them. Critter Hills gave the sanctuary space to care for a substantial herd, and cows now make up most of its residents. In 2021, the sanctuary took in roughly 40 cows from a neglect case in Sunrise, Florida.Cows are not the only animals rescued here. The sanctuary is home to 10 donkeys, 26 pigs, one turkey, 12 horses, a bison and a ‘very demanding’ water buffalo. “We encourage everyone to come meet the residents of CCFS and see that these animals are no different from the companion animals we all call friends.” The couple hosts monthly tours and annual public events to facilitate these encounters. They hope that meeting these animals will inspire people to treat them with compassion and leave animal products off their plates.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.standfirst: Aventaja en siete segundos al suizo Max Studer
articles.summary: Aventaja en siete segundos al suizo Max Studer,
articles.body: Alberto González se proclamó vencedor de la Copa del Mundo de triatlón de Tongyeong (Corea del Sur), superando con un tiempo de 50:03 en siete segundos al suizo Max Studer, mientras que David Castro terminó cuarto, a sólo nueve segundos del podio que completó el estadounidense Kevin Norland. Este triunfo de Alberto González llega sólo una semana después del bronce conseguido en la Copa del Mundo de Pekín, en la que Studer fue el vencedor. De esta forma, el malagueño regresa a lo más alto del podio de una Copa del Mundo por primera vez desde que lo alcanzase el 24 de marzo de 2024 en Hong Kong. La carrera, que se desarrolló en distancia esprint con 750 metros de natación, 19,8 kilómetros de ciclismo y 5 kilómetros de carrera a pie, estuvo marcada por la lluvia, que obligó a los triatletas a exigirse al máximo. Alberto González salió del segmento de natación en octava posición, cerca de los puestos de cabeza en los que consiguió situarse sobre la bicicleta con un grupo de nueve triatletas en el que no estaba Studer, que corriendo fue recortando distancias sin poder alcanzar al malagueño, que cruzó la meta en 50:03. El suizo lo hizo en 50:10 y Norland en 50:17. “Lo di todo desde el principio. No tuve miedo. Simplemente me bajé de la bici, me puse las zapatillas y seguí adelante, sin mirar atrás, y creo que está funcionando bien. Hoy estoy muy feliz de haber conseguido la victoria”, comentó González en meta. David Castro terminó cuarto con 50:26, a nueve segundos del bronce, mientras que los otros españoles fueron Roberto Sánchez Mantecón, décimo con 50:36; Eloy Canales Escribano decimotercero y Genís Grau en el puesto 42. En la categoría femenina, la china Xinyu Lin consiguió su segunda victoria consecutiva en la Copa del Mundo después de haberse impuesto también en Pekín. Segunda fue su compatriota Anqi Huang y tercera la francesa Mathilde Gautier. articles.title: Do abstaining voters hold the key to Brazil’s 2026 presidential election?
articles.summary: Some 21 percent of Brazilian adults did not cast a ballot in the first round of voting. Will they affect the run-off?
articles.body:
Sao Paulo, Brazil – The first time she voted in a Brazilian presidential election, in 2014, Larissa Campelo voted for centre-right Senator Aecio Neves. Four years later, in the next presidential race, she supported a centre-left candidate, former Sao Paulo Mayor Fernando Haddad.

But ahead of what is expected to be one of Brazil’s tightest presidential run-offs ever, the 30-year-old mother of one has decided she has had enough with politics.

She is abstaining from the vote on Sunday, just as she did during the first round of the election on October 4.

Voting is compulsory for most Brazilian adults. But Campelo is part of a historically large chunk of the electorate sitting out this year's presidential race.

Some 33.4 million Brazilian adults did not show up to vote in the first round, resulting in a 21 percent abstention rate, the highest for a general election since 1998.

“It’s my form of protest. I don’t want to dirty my hands with these candidates,” said Campelo, who lives in the Sao Paulo city of Araraquara.

“This isn’t apathy. It’s because I don’t feel there’s anyone qualified enough to earn my vote.”

But appealing to abstaining voters like Campelo may prove to be a path to victory in Sunday's run-off.

articles.title: Kamala Harris returns to campaign trail for US midterms amid speculation over 2028 presidential bid
articles.summary: Former US vice president Kamala Harris has returned to the campaign trail to support Democrats in closely contested races ahead of the November 3 midterm
articles.body: Former US vice president Kamala Harris has returned to the campaign trail to support Democrats in closely contested races ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, as speculation grows over whether she will make another bid for the White House in 2028.According to news agency Reuters, Harris, the Democratic Party's 2024 presidential nominee, is campaigning in Georgia, Mississippi, Nevada, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. She has made relatively few public appearances this year but is now stepping up efforts to help Democrats challenge Republican control of Congress.Harris began her campaign tour in Las Vegas on Tuesday, criticising President Donald Trump and his administration over what she described as its cruelty and incompetence. Speaking alongside Nevada gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford, she addressed members of the Culinary Workers Union."We got a serious fight in front of us," Harris said, accusing the Trump administration of being corrupt, callous and incompetent.Ford, Nevada's first Black attorney general, is seeking to become the state's governor. Harris said his election would make him the first Black governor west of the Mississippi River.Harris continued her campaign appearances in Mississippi, where she rallied supporters of Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom in Columbus. Colom is attempting to become the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Mississippi since 1982.He is facing Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in a closely contested race, Reuters reported.Addressing supporters, Harris encouraged young people not to let others' doubts limit their ambitions, drawing cheers from the crowd.Harris' popularity remains divided along party linesHarris' return to the campaign trail comes as both parties seek to mobilise voters ahead of the midterms. Trump has also been travelling across the country to campaign for Republican candidates facing competitive races.However, Harris continues to face challenges in winning support beyond the Democratic base.A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in June found that 39 per cent of Americans viewed her favourably. Her approval was significantly higher among Democrats, at 82 per cent, compared with 7 per cent among Republicans and 33 per cent among independents.Elaine Kamarck, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution and a member of the Democratic National Committee, said parties typically turn to their most prominent figures towards the end of an election campaign."At the end of a campaign, you bring out your heavy hitters," Kamarck was quoted as saying by Reuters, adding that this was the reason Harris and Trump were campaigning for their respective parties.Will Harris run for president again in 2028?Harris could emerge as one of the leading contenders if she decides to seek the Democratic presidential nomination in 2028. However, her political record includes two unsuccessful presidential campaigns.She lost to Trump in the 2024 election, while her first presidential campaign ended before the Democratic primaries began in 2020.A potential 2028 bid would also bring renewed scrutiny of the events surrounding the 2024 election, when then-president Joe Biden abandoned his re-election campaign amid concerns about his age and mental fitness, leaving Harris to take his place as the Democratic nominee.Harris later criticised Biden's decision to seek a second term as "reckless" in her memoir, 107 Days, named after the length of the presidential campaign she inherited.She has also become more vocal about the Biden administration's approach to Israel's war in Gaza.This month, Harris criticised the Israeli government's "horrific conduct" and said the US should have acted sooner and more forcefully.Harris says 2026 midterms come firstHarris has not ruled out another presidential run, but she has repeatedly emphasised the importance of the upcoming midterm elections.During an appearance on the video podcast Baby, This Is Keke Palmer this month, actor Keke Palmer asked Harris whether she would run for president again."Oh, girl, come on!" Harris replied, laughing. "I haven't decided yet."She then stressed that the immediate priority was the midterm elections."2028 don't matter if we don't do 2026 right," Harris said.Her return to the campaign trail is likely to keep her in the political spotlight as Democrats seek to regain congressional ground and potential candidates begin positioning themselves for the next presidential election.You use AI every day. articles.title: Las Vegas takes aim at notorious tourist trap as warnings appear along iconic Strip
articles.summary: Clark County billboard warnings tell Las Vegas Strip visitors that tipping costumed performers is not required after an alleged violent showgirl brawl occurred recently.
articles.body: Aggressive tipping demands from costumed performers on the Las Vegas Strip have prompted a warning from local authorities. Officials are reminding tourists that paying for street performances or character photos is never required, as FOX5 Las Vegas reported. Digital messages began appearing on billboards along the Strip on Friday, Oct. 16, with a direct warning to tourists. LAS VEGAS PRICES SQUEEZE EVERYDAY TRAVELERS AS POPULAR CITY EMBRACES EXPENSIVE MAKEOVER "When watching performances or taking a photo, tipping is NOT required," the signs read, according to reports. Clark County officials said the campaign is not intended to discourage voluntary tips, however. The initiative specifically targets performers who coerce visitors for cash or falsely imply that tipping is mandatory, FOX5 said. "It negatively impacts the economic lifeblood of not just Clark County — but the entire state tax base is dependent on the Las Vegas Strip," Clark County Commissioner Michael Naft told FOX5. Fox News Digital reached out to Clark County for further comment. Two visitors from North Carolina stopped for photos with three women dressed as showgirls outside Planet Hollywood on Sept. 30 and paid a $20 tip, Fox News Digital previously reported. After the tourists began walking away, performer Jennifer Ortiz allegedly followed them and demanded between $60 and $180 for the photos, according to an arrest report. The confrontation escalated into a fight that left both tourists injured. articles.title: Habitat destroyed by Cairngorms fire to be restored with government funding
articles.summary: The funding will also support habitat, species and river restoration, control of invasive non-native species and deer management across Scotland.
articles.body:
More than £1m is to be spent on nature recovery projects, including the restoration of habitats destroyed by a fire which ripped through a huge area of hillside in the Cairngorms.

The Scottish government funding will support habitat, species and river restoration, control of invasive non-native species and deer management across Scotland.

It includes £150,100 for recovery and nature restoration work following the Abernethy wildfire in the Cairngorms in July, to restore damaged habitats, help wildlife recover and reduce the risk of future wildfires.

Further funding will be provided to a range of other projects.

Support for species restoration, including native oyster restoration at various sites and habitat restoration on Islay for chough – rare members of the crow family

Habitat restoration in four national nature reserves

Announcing the funding at a summit in Armenia, Climate Action Secretary Gillian Martin said: "Nature underpins our health, wellbeing, economy and way of life, which is why restoring and protecting it is so important.

"This funding will support practical action, from improving habitats and rivers to tackling invasive species and supporting sustainable land management.

"It will also help recovery efforts in the Cairngorms following one of the most significant wildfire events in recent years, strengthening the resilience of these landscapes for the future."

She said being in Armenia alongside subnational governments and cities from around the world was a reminder that nature recovery was a shared global challenge.

"Scotland is committed to turning its ambitions for nature and climate into action, both at home and on the international stage, and this investment will help deliver real benefits for our environment, wildlife and communities," she added.

"The funding announced today by Ms Martin is a very welcome boost that will help us to kickstart nature recovery in the area.

"From replacing wildlife monitoring cameras that were damaged in the blaze to restoring a section of the Duack burn that was impacted by the emergency firebreaks, this funding will allow us to step up our work with our partners and enable swift action where it's most needed."

Stuart MacQuarrie, NatureScot director of nature and climate change, said: "This vital funding supports more people across Scotland to take action for nature.

"From helping to manage land for chough on Islay to supporting the restoration of native oysters and creating meadows for wildlife in our towns and cities, these local efforts combine to create a national drive to save nature.

"And by working to restore biodiverse habitats, manage deer sustainably and tackle the invasive species that threaten our native animal and plant life, we can look forward with hope, to a future where Scotland's nature is healthy and thriving."

articles.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after diagnosis
articles.summary: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.
articles.body:
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".

The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption.

Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.

"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.

"I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.

Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.

In Friday's video, Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.

Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.

Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.

articles.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visits China to inaugurate a new cross-border bridge
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited China on Saturday, inaugurating a new bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hoped to expand cooperation with his powerful neighbor.
articles.body: SEOUL, South Korea — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited China on Saturday, inaugurating a new bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hoped to expand cooperation with his powerful neighbor. Kim’s visit to China is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow in a united front against the United States under what he portrays as a “new Cold War.” It’s his first visit in a year. Kim arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong Saturday after crossing the newly opened bridge, according to South Korea’s Unification Ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua News Agency. Both sides promised to strengthen cooperation He met with Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of China’s Communist Party. The two toured a car factory, and promised to strengthen the bilateral relationship. Kim said his country “stands ready to work with China to carry forward their historical friendship and expand practical cooperation, thereby delivering tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries,” Xinhua said. Wang then accompanied Kim to the bridge to send him off, according to Xinhua. North Korean state media did not immediately report on Kim’s visit. New bridge was built to help expand trade between the countries Experts said the opening of the New Yalu River Bridge this month was a key symbol of strengthening ties between North Korea and China and reflected their intent to expand trade, as it is expected to accommodate two-way traffic around the clock, including container shipments and heavy cargo trucks. Kim has recently sought to strengthen ties with China, the North’s traditional main ally and economic lifeline, after years of prioritizing ties with Russia. He sent thousands of troops and conventional weapons to support President Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine, possibly in exchange for military and economic assistance. Kim’s visit timed to key battle anniversary in Korean War with China Kim’s latest visit to China is his sixth since taking power in late 2011 following the death of his father. The visit appears to be timed to underscore the strength of his ties with Beijing ahead of the Oct. 25 anniversary of China’s first major victory in the Korean War, which was days after Chinese troops crossed the Yalu River into North Korea in October 1950. The war began with North Korea’s surprise attack on the South in June 1950, prompting a U.N.-led coalition headed by the United States to intervene and push back the offensive. North Korea was backed primarily by Chinese forces, with assistance from the then-Soviet Union’s air force, before fighting ended with a 1953 armistice that left the peninsula technically at war. Kim said his visit on Saturday was also to memorialize those killed in the war, according to Xinhua. Chinese President Xi Jinping traveled to Pyongyang in June for a meeting with Kim. During their summit, Xi expressed Beijing’s willingness to expand bilateral cooperation in trade, agriculture, construction and technology, while Kim described ties with China as a top strategic priority. Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025, when he met with Xi and watched a military parade alongside Putin and other foreign leaders. Kim has maintained a hard line toward Seoul and has so far rebuffed a proposal from U.S. President Donald Trump to revive their diplomacy, which broke down in 2019 during Trump’s first term. Kim’s government has called for Washington to abandon its “hostile policy” and drop demands for the North’s denuclearization as a precondition for renewed talks. South Korea’s liberal government, which favors engagement with the North, hopes renewed talks between Washington and Pyongyang will thaw inter-Korean relations, and has also urged China to play a “constructive” role in resolving the standoff. Seoul’s spy agency told lawmakers last month that it saw a 50% possibility of a meeting between Trump and Kim on the sidelines of next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, summit in Shenzhen, China. “From Seoul’s perspective, if North Korea focuses more on economic development than military buildup and threats, that would be positive for diplomacy and security,” said Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul. “But if Kim can extract ever more benefits from China and Russia, it is unclear what Seoul could offer that would be worth the political risks Pyongyang attaches to exchanges with a more prosperous, globalized, and free Korea.”

articles.title: Thousands still without power as UK braces for worst of Storm Boelo
articles.summary: Strong winds and rain will continue across the UK due to the storm, the Met Office has warned.
articles.body:
Thousands of homes are still without power as the UK faces its second storm in as many days, with worse weather approaching some parts of the country.

Storm Boelo, following Storm Austen, has brought strong winds and heavy showers, with widespread gusts of 60 to 70mph expected to hit Scotland from Saturday evening.

Amber wind warnings from the Met Office will come into force from 21:00 BST for parts of Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England, bringing an increased risk of travel disruption and potential risk to life.

In south-west England, more than 6,000 properties have remained without power after being hit the hardest by Storm Austen, according to National Grid figures.

The National Grid said on Saturday that 117,320 properties had been restored with power supplies since the beginning of the storm.

However, thousands have been left without power across the south-west, including 141 properties near Beaminster in Dorset, 384 near Whimple in East Devon, and 168 near Penhale in Cornwall.

Storm Boelo is set to cause disruption throughout the weekend, with the amber warning in Scotland due to stay in place for 24 hours.

Forecasters have warned of strong winds with gusts to 80mph expected in exposed coastal areas.

These winds could cause power cuts, flying debris, damage to buildings and trees, travel disruption and danger to life from large waves, the Met Office said.

The strongest winds will affect western Scotland first on Saturday evening, before spreading eastwards overnight and through Sunday.

The Met Office has warned that being outside in high winds could make people "more vulnerable to injury", stating: "Stay indoors as much as possible. If you do go out, try not to walk, or shelter, close to buildings and trees."

Parts of Northern Ireland have also been issued with an amber warning, from 21:00 on Saturday to 10:00 on Sunday.

Meanwhile, yellow rain warnings have been issued for the south-west, north-west and south-east of England, the West Midlands and Wales until 23:00 on Saturday.

Much of the north of England and Scotland has a yellow wind warning in place, which is set to last until 21:00 on Sunday, and Northern Ireland's yellow wind warning will be in place until midday on Sunday.

Jason Kelly, the Met Office's chief forecaster, said: "People should prepare for the potential for disruption, particularly to travel and power supplies. Secure loose items outside, plan ahead if you are travelling and keep up to date with the latest forecast and warnings for your area."

articles.title: More than 2,000 forced from homes in Hebron amid Israel’s West Bank raids
articles.summary: Palestinians in Hebron are ‘living in fear’ with the city closed, while Israeli forces arrest dozens across the West Bank.
articles.body:
Israel has imposed a lockdown and displaced thousands of Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as the military conducts raids in the occupied West Bank following the deaths of two Israeli soldiers.

This comes as the Palestinian Authority (PA) on Saturday called for international pressure on Israel to protect Hebron’s residents, who said soldiers announced evacuation orders over loudspeakers late at night, leaving them with no time to prepare and few places to move to.

Hebron’s mayor Yousef al-Ja’bari told Al Jazeera that 2,200 people had been forced from their homes as hundreds of Israeli raids took place since Friday’s attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli army reserve base. The two Palestinians were killed , as well as the two Israeli soldiers.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu then ordered a “ full lockdown ” of the West Bank following the attack.

Mayor al-Ja’bari said on Saturday that Hebron residents can neither enter nor leave the city.

Israeli soldiers also fired a stun grenade at Al Jazeera journalists near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint in Hebron, as they documented an Israeli operation to bulldoze homes and vehicles in the area.

The Israeli military carried out raids across at least 15 areas of the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported.

Those targeted include Jenin and Nablus in the north; Ramallah, Al-Bireh, Birzeit, and occupied East Jerusalem in the centre; and Bethlehem in the south.

Israeli forces have arrested about 70 Palestinians in raids across the West Bank , the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society said.

The PA, which governs the West Bank, called Israel’s actions “collective punishment” , citing the demolition of homes, forced displacement of entire neighbourhoods, and the “closure and siege of Palestinian cities”, and urged the international community to intervene, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Meanwhile, Hamas said in a statement that the “campaigns and escalations carried out by the occupation and its criminal settlers against our people will only fuel further outrage”.

Around 200,000 Palestinians live in the city of Hebron itself, and a further 600,000 in Hebron governorate, making it the West Bank’s most populous governorate.

Those 800,000 Palestinians in Hebron governorate are “ now under siege , with all entrances and exits closed since morning”, Issa Amro, a Palestinian activist and political analyst based in Hebron, told Al Jazeera.

“Inside the city, there is no safe place for anyone to hide … the city is really in fear,” Amro said.

Israeli politicians are trying to “capitalise” on the attack ahead of parliamentary elections on October 27 , Al Jazeera’s West Bank correspondent Nour Odeh said.

“Netanyahu, his Likud party, and his allies in this right-wing coalition are behind in the polls,” said Odeh, so in response they are “trying to put up a brave front, saying they’re combating Palestinians”.

Just days before Israelis are set to vote, Netanyahu avoided answering whether he planned to dismantle the PA, but said a “ big surprise” awaits the organisation .
